area: Sessions and resume, worktrees and their cleanup, sandboxing, checkpoints, background tasks, and what carries between sessions in Claude Code (as of 2026-09-02)

facts.behavior: Resumes the most recent interactive session in the current directory
facts.limits: Skips background sessions and sessions whose first prompt was /loop; excludes claude -p and Agent SDK sessions from the picker/--continue (resume those via claude --resume <session-id>), unless combined with -p (claude -p --continue includes -p, SDK, and /loop sessions but still skips background sessions)

facts.behavior: claude --resume with no argument opens the interactive session picker; claude --resume <name> resumes the named session directly if the name matches exactly; claude --resume <session-id> resumes by ID and can be run from any directory
facts.limits: Cross-project ID lookup checks the current project + its worktrees first, then every other project on the machine, but only resolves when exactly one other project holds a transcript with messages for that ID — a duplicate makes it report not-found rather than guess

facts.behavior: A resumed session restores: full conversation history including tool calls/results; the model it was using; the agent (system prompt, tool restrictions, model) if started with --agent or the agent setting; the permission mode (with documented exceptions); an active goal (turn count/timer/spend baseline reset); and scheduled tasks that haven't expired
facts.limits: Model isn't restored when retired, disallowed by availableModels, or overridden by --model/an ANTHROPIC_MODEL-family env var at relaunch; background Bash and monitor tasks are explicitly NOT restored

facts.feature: Launch flags not restored on resume
facts.behavior: Not every configuration flag from the original launch is restored on resume
facts.limits: --mcp-config, --settings, --plugin-dir, --fallback-model, and directories added with --add-dir must be passed again explicitly; directories added mid-session with /add-dir aren't restored either (though the picker still uses them to locate the session). Standard settings.json/settings.local.json ARE re-read automatically, so config living there doesn't need to be re-passed

facts.behavior: Terminal resumes (claude --continue, claude --resume <id>, claude --resume <name> matching one session) restore the permission mode the session ended in, except several documented cases (e.g. a session that ended in bypassPermissions or plan mode falls back to whatever mode a new session would start in). Resuming via the session picker or /resume never restores the stored mode — it starts in whatever mode a new session/the current session is already in
facts.limits: Behavior differs by entry path (terminal vs. non-interactive -p vs. VS Code vs. picker vs. /resume); pass --permission-mode or --dangerously-skip-permissions to override

facts.behavior: On a Pro/Max plan, resuming a session inactive for more than ~1 hour and over 100,000 tokens opens a dialog before your first message, offering 'Resume from summary' (runs /compact immediately), 'Resume full session as-is', or 'Don't ask me again'
facts.limits: Triggers only when the prompt cache has expired for that inactive/large session; whichever option is picked, the next request reprocesses the full history once

facts.behavior: By default the picker shows sessions from the current worktree (background sessions marked 'bg') plus sessions elsewhere that added the current directory with /add-dir; Ctrl+W widens to all worktrees of the repository, Ctrl+A widens to every project on the machine, Ctrl+B filters to the current git branch
facts.limits: Sessions whose first prompt was /loop never appear in the picker (and claude --continue skips them); running /loop later in a conversation does not hide it

facts.behavior: /branch (or claude --continue/--resume --fork-session) copies the conversation so far into a new session ID and switches into it, leaving the original session's transcript unchanged and still in the picker
facts.limits: Inherits: conversation history up to the branch point, 'allow for this session' permission grants (only when branching stays in the same process — a --fork-session into a new process starts without them), in-flight background subagents/Bash (their output lands in the new branch), and the Remote Control connection

facts.behavior: Sessions can be named via -n/--name at startup, /rename during a session, Ctrl+R in the picker, or auto-titled on plan-accept; starting or renaming into a name another live session on the machine already holds auto-renames the newcomer to a two-word-suffix variant (e.g. auth-refactor-graceful-unicorn) and tells you
facts.limits: Doesn't dedupe AI-generated titles, default display names, or the --name of a background/-p session at startup; can't rename a session running on an older Claude Code version

facts.behavior: Transcripts are stored as JSONL at ~/.claude/projects/<project>/<session-id>.jsonl by default, one JSON object per line (message, tool use, or metadata entry)
facts.limits: The entry format is internal and changes between versions, so scripts should use /export, claude -p --output-format json/stream-json, the transcript_path field hooks receive, or the Agent SDK instead of parsing the JSONL directly

facts.behavior: CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR moves storage off ~/.claude; cleanupPeriodDays changes the default 30-day retention; CLAUDE_CODE_SKIP_PROMPT_HISTORY suppresses transcript writes in all modes; --no-session-persistence suppresses writes for one non-interactive run
facts.limits: --no-session-persistence only works with claude -p

facts.behavior: Starts a fresh, empty context; Claude Code saves the previous conversation, resumable via /resume or, within the same process, via the rewind menu's previous-session entry
facts.limits: With no argument the new conversation keeps a name set with --name/--rename but not an AI-generated title; naming while clearing (e.g. /clear release-prep) names the conversation being left instead

facts.behavior: Creates a git worktree and starts Claude in it, by default under .claude/worktrees/<name>/ at the repo root on a new branch named worktree-<name>; omitting a name auto-generates one
facts.limits: Requires a git repository (non-git VCS needs a WorktreeCreate hook); interactive runs require prior workspace trust in that directory or --worktree exits with an error; non-interactive -p skips the trust check

facts.behavior: On exiting an interactive worktree session, a clean unnamed session's worktree (dir + branch) is removed automatically; a named session prompts first; a worktree containing changed/untracked files or new commits always prompts to keep or remove
facts.limits: Non-interactive -p runs get no exit prompt and no cleanup — the lock taken at creation stays until a later stale-lock sweep releases it; manual cleanup is git worktree remove (git worktree unlock first if locked)

facts.feature: Periodic sweep of subagent and background-session worktrees
facts.behavior: A periodic sweep removes worktrees Claude created for subagents and background sessions once older than the cleanupPeriodDays setting, following the same retention rules as other cleaned-up data
facts.limits: Leaves a worktree in place if it holds changed/untracked files or unpushed commits, if filter drivers can't be determined, if it belongs to a --worktree session not yet backgrounded, or if the user created it themselves with git worktree add; a lock from a killed session is released by the sweep, but a lock the user set manually with git worktree lock never is

facts.behavior: While a session is isolated in a worktree, Claude Code blocks: (1) an Edit/Write/NotebookEdit targeting a path in the main checkout; (2) a Bash/PowerShell/Monitor command whose working directory resolves to, or can't be verified to stay outside, the main checkout; (3) a Bash/Monitor command that redirects git into the main checkout (via git -C, --git-dir, GIT_DIR/GIT_WORK_TREE, or a prior cd); (4) a Bash/Monitor command shape it can't verify stays inside the worktree (e.g. brace expansion, heredocs with unquoted delimiters)
facts.limits: Applies to every subagent spawned from the isolated session, foreground or background, interactive or background session; PowerShell only gets check (2). Documentation states plainly: 'You can't turn this check off'

facts.behavior: A .gitignore-syntax file at the project root that copies matching gitignored files (e.g. .env, config/secrets.json) into every new worktree Claude Code creates with git
facts.limits: Only files that both match a pattern AND are gitignored are copied (tracked files never duplicated); not processed at all when a WorktreeCreate hook replaces the default git logic for non-git VCS — copy files inside the hook script instead

facts.feature: What worktrees share with the main checkout
facts.behavior: A worktree gets its own files and branch but shares the repository's .git directory (so git commit etc. work under sandboxing), project-scope plugins installed from the main checkout, and 'don't ask again' permission approvals (saved to the main checkout's .claude/settings.local.json, applying to and surviving past the worktree's removal)
facts.limits: On Windows and other cases where Claude Code doesn't use the repo root, an approval instead stays local to that worktree only

facts.behavior: Resuming a session that was inside a worktree returns it to that worktree (covers interactive resume, -p --continue/--resume, and the Agent SDK); Claude Code first verifies the worktree is still a separate checkout and declines to re-enter one that fails the check
facts.limits: If the worktree directory no longer exists, the session resumes in the launch directory instead and the worktree binding is cleared; --fork-session always starts in the launch directory, leaving the original session's worktree untouched

facts.behavior: Controls which branch new worktrees branch from: 'fresh' (default) branches from the repository's default branch on the remote; 'head' branches from the current local HEAD, carrying unpushed commits/feature-branch state
facts.limits: Cannot be set to an arbitrary existing branch name — create such a worktree with git directly instead

facts.behavior: Provides OS-level filesystem and network isolation for shell commands so Claude can run most commands without stopping for per-command approval; enabled via the /sandbox panel or the sandbox.enabled setting (project-local by default, or user-wide/org-managed)
facts.limits: Built in, runs on macOS, Linux, and WSL2 only; native Windows is not supported (run inside WSL2 instead); on Linux/WSL2 requires the bubblewrap and socat packages

facts.behavior: Auto-allow mode runs sandboxable commands inside the sandbox and approves them automatically without prompting; Regular permissions mode routes all Bash commands through the normal permission flow even when sandboxed
facts.limits: Even in auto-allow: explicit deny rules always apply, rm/rmdir targeting a critical path still goes through the regular permission flow, content-scoped ask rules like Bash(git push *) still force a prompt, and a bare Bash/Bash(*) ask rule is skipped for sandboxed commands except in plan mode, where it still prompts (including for read-only commands)

facts.behavior: Sandboxed commands get read+write access to the current working directory, any directories added with --add-dir/permissions.additionalDirectories, and the session temp directory; read access to the entire computer except denied paths — this default still allows reading credential files such as ~/.aws/credentials and ~/.ssh/
facts.limits: Cannot write outside those allowed directories without explicit sandbox.filesystem.allowWrite configuration; use sandbox.credentials or denyRead to block credential-file reads, which are NOT blocked by default

facts.behavior: Inside directories a sandboxed command can otherwise write to, the sandbox always denies writes to Claude Code's own config/code paths: .claude settings files, .claude/skills, .claude/agents, .claude/commands, .claude/hooks, .mcp.json, .claude/workflows, .claude/scheduled_tasks.json, shell startup files (.bashrc/.zshrc), .gitconfig, .vscode/.idea, .git/hooks and .git/config, files that would turn the working dir into a bare git repo, and most of ~/.claude including .claude.json and .credentials.json
facts.limits: There is no way to exempt one of these paths — an allowWrite entry or Edit allow rule covering the path does not lift the protection; the only way to disable it is sandbox.filesystem.disabled, which turns off filesystem isolation entirely for every path

facts.behavior: Network access goes through a proxy outside the sandbox; Claude Code pre-allows no domains by default. The first time a command needs a new domain it prompts for approval (or the auto-mode classifier decides); approving Yes allows the host for the rest of the session, and 'Yes, and don't ask again' saves a WebFetch(domain:...) allow rule to local settings for future sessions
facts.limits: By default the proxy does not terminate or inspect TLS, so encrypted contents aren't examined and a broadly-allowed domain (e.g. github.com) can potentially be abused via domain fronting for exfiltration; strictAllowlist/allowManagedDomainsOnly can deny instead of prompt but only take effect from user/managed/CLI --settings, never from repo .claude/settings.json or settings.local.json

facts.behavior: When a command can't run inside the sandbox, Claude Code reports the violation and Claude may retry the command with the dangerouslyDisableSandbox parameter, which runs it outside the sandbox through the normal permission flow (prompt in Manual mode, classifier in auto mode)
facts.limits: Can be fully disabled by setting allowUnsandboxedCommands: false ('Strict sandbox mode'), after which the parameter is ignored entirely and every command must run sandboxed or be explicitly listed in excludedCommands

facts.feature: Sandbox scope — tools and processes it does NOT cover
facts.behavior: The sandbox isolates Bash subprocesses only. Built-in file tools (Read, Edit, Write) go through the permission system directly, not the sandbox. Computer use runs on the real desktop, not an isolated environment, gated only by per-app permission prompts. Subagents run in the same process and inherit the parent session's sandbox configuration
facts.limits: Sandboxed Bash commands inherit the parent process environment, including credentials set there, by default unless sandbox.credentials or CLAUDE_CODE_SUBPROCESS_ENV_SCRUB strip them

facts.feature: Sandboxing is not a complete security boundary
facts.behavior: Documentation states directly: 'Sandboxing reduces risk but is not a complete isolation boundary. Review the limitations below before relying on it as a hard security control.' Named risks include no TLS content inspection by default, allowUnixSockets potentially granting host access (e.g. the Docker socket), overly broad filesystem writes enabling privilege escalation, enableWeakerNestedSandbox weakening Linux isolation, and allowAppleEvents removing code-execution isolation on macOS
facts.limits: n/a — this is the documentation's own stated limitation

facts.behavior: Claude Code automatically captures the state of code before each user prompt via its file editing tools; every user prompt creates a new checkpoint, and checkpoints are saved with the conversation so /rewind still works after resuming a session
facts.limits: Keeps file snapshots for only the 100 most recent checkpoints in a session; discarding an older checkpoint deletes snapshot files no remaining checkpoint references, except each file's first snapshot (kept for the VS Code extension's session-diff baseline)

facts.behavior: Opened via /rewind, or Esc twice on an empty prompt input; lists each prompt sent during the session and offers Restore code and conversation, Restore conversation, Restore code, Summarize from here, Summarize up to here, or Never mind
facts.limits: The two code-restore options appear only when the selected checkpoint has tracked file changes to revert; summarizing doesn't change files on disk and the original messages stay in the transcript

facts.behavior: Claude Code deletes checkpoints along with their sessions after 30 days by default
facts.limits: Period is changeable via the cleanupPeriodDays setting

facts.behavior: Checkpointing does not track files modified by bash commands such as rm, mv, or cp — only direct edits made through Claude's file editing tools are tracked
facts.limits: Such bash-driven file modifications cannot be undone through /rewind

facts.feature: Checkpointing limitation — subagent edits usually not restored
facts.behavior: A subagent's file edits are usually not captured in the parent session's checkpoints. The one exception: a skill with context: fork running in the foreground (background: false, or a case the skills page forces to foreground) edits the working tree during the parent's own turn and IS captured by rewind
facts.limits: Every other subagent case — including a background forked skill (the default) and a background /code-review --fix run — is NOT restored by rewind; use git to revert those edits

facts.feature: Checkpointing limitation — external, concurrent, and linked-file changes
facts.behavior: Checkpointing only tracks files edited within the current session: manual changes made outside Claude Code and edits from other concurrent sessions normally aren't captured unless they touch the same files. Restoring code also skips any tracked path that is a symlink or hard link, showing a 'Restored the code, but skipped N files' warning
facts.limits: Skipped symlinked/hard-linked files keep their current contents and must be reverted manually (e.g. by asking Claude to reverse the specific edit)

facts.feature: Checkpointing is not a replacement for version control
facts.behavior: Documentation states directly: checkpoints 'are designed for quick, session-level recovery. For permanent version history and collaboration, continue using version control, such as Git, for commits, branches, and long-term history.'
facts.limits: n/a — stated design limitation

facts.behavior: A Bash command can be run in the background (by prompting Claude, or pressing Ctrl+B on a running invocation); Claude Code runs it asynchronously, returns a background task ID immediately, writes output to a file Claude retrieves via the Read tool, and keeps responding to new prompts while it runs
facts.limits: Automatically terminated if output exceeds 5GB; on macOS/Linux, terminated on OS memory-pressure signal once the session has been idle 30+ minutes and no turn/subagent is running (disable via CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_BG_SHELL_PRESSURE_REAP); background commands owned by a subagent are instead terminated after 60 minutes by default (configurable via CLAUDE_SUBAGENT_BG_SHELL_MAX_MS), and end when a foreground subagent that owns one gives its final response

facts.behavior: Background tasks are automatically cleaned up when Claude Code exits; backgrounding the session itself (instead of exiting) hands them to the background session, where they keep running
facts.limits: To disable background task functionality entirely, set CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_BACKGROUND_TASKS=1

facts.behavior: Claude's to-do checklist persists across context compactions within a session; can be shared across sessions by setting CLAUDE_CODE_TASK_LIST_ID to a named directory under ~/.claude/tasks/
facts.limits: On Opus 4.8, Sonnet 5, Fable 5, Mythos 5, and later, Claude tracks multi-step work without a written checklist by default and the tools that fill this list aren't provided, so it stays empty unless CLAUDE_CODE_ENABLE_TODO_TOOLS=1 or another opt-in is set

facts.behavior: Claude Code keeps a history of typed prompts; Up-arrow recall reaches prompts from past sessions of the same project, stored per working directory
facts.limits: Running /clear starts a new session for history purposes — recall then lists the new session's prompts first, with earlier sessions' prompts after; submitting the same prompt twice in a row records only one history entry

facts.behavior: Claude Code shows a one-line recap of what happened in the session, generated in the background once at least 3 minutes have passed since the last completed turn and the terminal is unfocused; /recap generates one on demand, capped at 400 characters
facts.limits: Only appears once the session has at least 3 turns, never twice in a row, and never in non-interactive mode; can be turned off via /config

facts.behavior: When a claude.ai usage limit stops Claude mid-task, an open interactive session (signed in with a claude.ai subscription) waits and automatically continues the task once the limit resets, sending a fixed continuation prompt rather than resending the last message
facts.limits: On, by default, in interactive sessions only — not for background sessions, -p runs, API keys, cloud providers/usage-based billing, or an LLM gateway without a saved claude.ai login; re-arms at most twice in a row on repeated hits before stopping; can be turned off via autoContinueAtUsageLimit setting

facts.behavior: --bg starts an interactive session in the background and returns immediately, printing an id; claude attach <id> reopens it in the terminal, claude agents lists background agents, claude logs <id> prints recent output, claude stop|kill <id> stops one while keeping its conversation resumable, claude rm <id> deletes a background session and its worktree 'when that is safe', claude respawn restarts a background session (or all, with --all) on the current Claude Code version
facts.limits: rm and stop/kill work on sessions that have already exited; --resume <session-id> --bg either continues that session in the background under the same ID, or starts a copy and says so if the session is already running

facts.behavior: When resuming, creates a new session ID instead of reusing the original; used with --resume or --continue
facts.limits: n/a — see the worktrees/sessions docs for how forking interacts with worktree bindings and permission grants

facts.behavior: Use a specific session ID for the conversation (must be a valid UUID)
facts.limits: n/a

facts.behavior: Disables session persistence — the session will not be saved to disk and cannot be resumed
facts.limits: Only works with --print (non-interactive mode)

facts.behavior: Create a tmux session for the worktree; uses iTerm2 native panes when available, or --tmux=classic for traditional tmux
facts.limits: Requires --worktree

facts.behavior: Bypass all permission checks; --allow-dangerously-skip-permissions makes bypass available as an option without enabling it by default
facts.limits: Per --help, 'Recommended only for sandboxes with no internet access'; per the sandboxing doc, it is blocked when running as root/sudo on Linux/macOS unless inside a recognized sandbox

facts.behavior: Removes the built-in tools that run commands or code (Bash, PowerShell, REPL, and other code-running tools) and WebFetch unless --tools names them; ignores user, project, and local settings files (managed settings and --settings still apply; add --strict-mcp-config to also skip MCP servers); confines file tools to the working directories (--add-dir included); refuses bypassPermissions
facts.limits: Only a person or the configured permission handler can approve writes to settings, git, and tool-configuration files under --restricted

facts.behavior: Starts with all customizations disabled — CLAUDE.md, skills, plugins, hooks, MCP servers, custom commands and agents, output styles, workflows, custom themes, keybindings, and more — for troubleshooting a broken configuration; sets CLAUDE_CODE_SAFE_MODE=1
facts.limits: Admin-managed (policy) settings still apply; auth, model selection, built-in tools, and permissions work normally

facts.behavior: Minimal mode: skips hooks, LSP, plugin sync, attribution, auto-memory, background prefetches, keychain reads, and CLAUDE.md auto-discovery; sets CLAUDE_CODE_SIMPLE=1
facts.limits: Anthropic auth is strictly ANTHROPIC_API_KEY or apiKeyHelper via --settings (OAuth and keychain are never read); skills still resolve via /skill-name; context (CLAUDE.md, MCP, settings, agents) must be provided explicitly via flags

facts.behavior: Setting CLAUDE_CODE_PROJECT_DIR_NAME (alongside CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR) makes Claude Code store that session's transcripts AND its auto memory under a chosen name instead of one derived from the full working-directory path
facts.limits: Only takes effect when CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR is also set; must be 1-64 letters/digits/hyphens/underscores (no Windows device names); must be set in the shell environment that starts claude (an env block in a settings file can't set it)

facts.behavior: Claude can create or switch worktrees mid-session by calling the EnterWorktree tool with a target path, and leave one with ExitWorktree; the previous worktree stays on disk untouched
facts.limits: Entering a path outside the repository's .claude/worktrees/ requires user approval first — an EnterWorktree permission rule or 'don't ask again' does not suppress this prompt; only bypassPermissions mode skips it
